collection.credit:
* V9 "Age of Terrible Ideas": event prose, material applications,
  trial and consequence branches by ChatGPT. Core requests for intense
  conflict, fights, false guilt, courts, imprisonment, reconciliation,
  and the sixteen specific bizarre materials by Lorsieab2.

items.text: The families share custody of the spoon, then immediately argue over who gets it on Tuesdays.
The elder carves two replicas. Both families claim the replica is inferior to the original.
The rival says, 'I still hate your cooking.' The cook says, 'At least you've finally tasted it.'

intro.name: The spoon
intro.text: A ceremonial wooden spoon has vanished from the communal kitchen. It is worth almost nothing, except that two families have argued about its ownership for years. A cook accuses a rival of stealing it. The rival shouts, 'I WOULD RATHER EAT CAVE GUANO THAN TOUCH YOUR SPOON!'

text_only.reason: an object goes missing, not a villager

question.name: The case
question.text: A village leader appoints an impartial elder to hear the case.

choices.label: Let both sides present their evidence formally.

w1.text: A child saw someone with a spoon but cannot identify which spoon.

w2.text: A nursing mother says she borrowed a DIFFERENT spoon to prepare food, and resents being treated as a criminal for it.

w3.text: A tired father admits he moved the spoon while cleaning.

w4.text: An elder confesses because (elder.he/she) dislikes seeing people argue, but has no actual knowledge of the theft.

text_only.reason: a trait of a text figure, not a game preference

s1.text: The spoon is found behind a shelf.

s2.text: It is discovered inside a hollow loaf of bread. Nobody can explain why.

s3.text: A broken spoon is found, but it is not the missing one.

s4.text: The cook had placed it in a safe box and forgotten.

m1.text: The families agree to share the spoon on festival days.

m2.text: Both reject mediation and demand a verdict.

m3.text: One family offers to make a second spoon. The other insists the original has sentimental value.

m4.text: The mediator admits the spoon looks like every other spoon on Isola.

trial.name: The trial
trial.text: The judge asks for evidence, not insults. The cook produces a diagram of the crime scene that is mostly angry arrows. The rival produces four witnesses who can only testify that the cook is 'annoying.'

t1.text: A credible witness proves the rival borrowed the spoon and forgot to return it. The judge orders its return and an apology.

t2.text: The evidence is contradictory. No guilt is established.

t3.text: The rival admits deliberately hiding the spoon out of spite.

t4.text: The cook admits inventing the accusation to humiliate the rival.

confusion.text: The judge adjourns until the witnesses can distinguish a soup spoon from a ceremonial spoon. A child asks whether the judge is paid. 'No,' says the judge. 'Clearly.'

found.text: The spoon is returned. The accuser must correct the public allegation. The accused may remain angry. A happy ending is not mandatory.

wrong_guilt.name: Wrong guilt
wrong_guilt.text: A villager confesses to an act (confessor.he/she) did not commit, either from fear, misplaced responsibility, or a desire to end the hearing. The judge refuses to convict without corroboration. The confession is withdrawn or investigated, and the villager is treated kindly.

accountability.text:
The wrongdoer faces restitution and a fair hearing.
The judge refuses to imprison anyone over a spoon merely to satisfy the crowd.
